findings.evidence: Both proofs are `rw [DihedralGroup.exponent]; decide` against `Mathlib/GroupTheory/SpecificGroups/Dihedral.lean:211` (`Monoid.exponent (DihedralGroup n) = lcm n 2`); neither statement nor proof mentions anything from `Dixon/Prime.lean`. `grep -rn "Monoid.exponent" TauCeti` shows no other in-repo consumer, and the file's own imports (line 8-9) are the whole Dixon chain.
findings.fix: Move both to a new `TauCeti/GroupTheory/SpecificGroups/Dihedral.lean` importing only `Mathlib.GroupTheory.SpecificGroups.Dihedral`, mirroring Mathlib's path (`TauCeti/GroupTheory/` already exists), and import that from `Dixon/Dihedral.lean`.
findings.issue: `exponent_dihedralGroup_four` (line 30) and `exponent_dihedralGroup_three` (line 74) are pure group theory — numeric specializations of `DihedralGroup.exponent` — with no dependence on representations, characters, or Dixon primes, yet they are public `@[simp]` lemmas in the root `TauCeti` namespace exported from a character-table module. Using either now requires pulling in Maschke, `PrimesCongruentOne`, and `Values.lean` (complex character values).

summary: Placement and imports are otherwise sound — the Dixon material sits where the roadmap prescribes and every import is used and narrow — but two general dihedral group-theory facts are published as global @[simp] lemmas from a character-table module.
